FAQ

If you’ve got questions [about anything], you’ve come to the right place. 

What is Scribd?

Scribd is the world's library of ideas, with over [300M] documents and counting. Find and upload content on every topic and niche, from academic papers and legal documents to DIY hobbies, manuals, and more.
To share a document to Scribd, you must be the creator of or have the permission of the document’s creator. Read more on that in our Copyright FAQs.

Do I need a subscription to access Scribd?

No subscription is required – you can read and upload without a subscription. With a subscription, you can download documents and enjoy an ad-free experience.

What are the benefits of paying for a Scribd subscription?

For just [$11.99/month] you will enjoy the following benefits:
  • Ad-free access to explore and download from a library of [300M+] documents
  • Download documents to read offline
  • Complimentary access to millions of community-uploaded presentations through Slideshare
  • Looking for audiobooks and ebooks? Visit Everand

Can I upload and share documents on Scribd?

Yes, you can upload documents to reach a global community of millions of users. You can even embed your documents in your own site. If you have more questions on how to upload or what can be uploaded, please visit our help center.

How does Scribd handle copyright infringement?

At Scribd, we take copyright infringement very seriously. Copyright infringement is illegal and not permitted on Scribd under any circumstances. When we receive a valid claim of copyright infringement, we expeditiously remove infringing material and terminate repeat infringers pursuant to a "three-strikes" policy.

Scribd, Inc. has also developed BookID, an automated copyright protection system that helps to safeguard intellectual property. BookID scans every document uploaded to Scribd and removes those with the same, or a substantially similar, fingerprint. BookID intermittently scans the entire Scribd library to remove matching content uploaded before fingerprinting.

How can I report copyright infringement to Scribd?

Content on Scribd.com and in the Scribd app is directly uploaded by Scribd users without pre-approval by Scribd. Scribd complies with all applicable provisions of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) of 1998. Since Scribd is based in the United States, a notification that complies with DMCA criteria is the minimum that Scribd can accept as proof-of-copyright, even if your country operates under different laws. Scribd cannot process notifications that disregard DMCA criteria and provide incomplete information.

To report an infringement of your copyright on Scribd, use the DMCA form.

To learn more about our copyright policies, please visit our full FAQ section.

How do I cancel my subscription?

You can cancel your subscription at any time by visiting your Account Settings. If you cancel your subscription, you’ll have access to your benefits until any remaining subscription time expires.
Have more questions? Visit our Help & FAQs.
